name: fanqiang
one_liner: A library of free tools, apps, and guides that help people in countries with heavy internet censorship (most notably China) get around the block and reach the open internet.
buyer: Not a commercial buyer situation — this is volunteer-run circumvention software aimed at ordinary citizens under censorship, not a paying customer segment.
business_use_cases: A press-freedom or human-rights nonprofit references it when advising journalists and activists on safe internet access.
An individual living under internet censorship uses the guides to reach international news and communication tools.
A digital-rights researcher studies it as a case study of grassroots censorship-circumvention tooling.

money_ideas.idea: No legitimate outside-operator monetization path — building a paid product around censorship circumvention raises real legal and ethical risk depending on jurisdiction, and this project itself is donation/volunteer-run for good reason.

steal_this: There's no honest weekend business here — this is humanitarian infrastructure, not a monetizable opportunity, and treating it as one would be the wrong call.
